title: Normosol-R vs Lactated Ringers in the Critically Ill: A Randomized Trial
summary: A single-center pragmatic cluster-randomized multiple-crossover study assigned 2,084 critically ill adults to Normosol-R or lactated Ringer's. Mean plasma bicarbonate through day 7 did not differ (difference -0.12 mmol/dL; 95% CI -0.61 to 0.36; P=.61). New kidney replacement therapy occurred in 6.0% versus 5.0% and 30-day death in 16.3% versus 16.0%, without established differences.
findings: Bicarbonate difference -0.12 mmol/dL (95% CI -0.61 to 0.36; P=.61).
New kidney replacement therapy 6.0% versus 5.0%, difference 1.0% (95% CI -1.2% to 3.1%).
Detailed adverse-event data not reported in the reviewed abstract.
population: Critically ill adults in one academic center; 2,084 enrolled.
limitations: Single-center ICU trial with a biochemical primary endpoint; absence of significant differences does not prove equivalence. Primary abstract reviewed; linked open-access full text was not reviewed end-to-end.
whyItMatters: This does not support replacing lactated Ringer's with Normosol-R to improve outcomes in eligible critically ill adults. It compares two balanced crystalloids, not saline versus a balanced fluid.
evidenceNotes: Primary PubMed abstract PMID 39971001 DOI 10.1016/j.chest.2025.02.008 reviewed, Epub February 17, 2025 versus August print. Legal full text linked but not reviewed. No verified correction found in targeted search.
primaryEndpoint: Mean plasma bicarbonate concentration through day 7.
